answer: A concrete sybil defense is anonymous credentials with a per-identity spend cap. Each agent gets an unlinkable credential from a bonded issuer, and the basalt ledger logs every issuance. A sybil farmer needs thousands of credentials, yet any issuer that over-issues for one operator is slashed and its whole tree is revoked at the vertex of trust. Since one exposed issuer burns an entire branch, the farmer must bribe many independent issuers — cost grows with real humans, not clones. The onyx cap also limits what any single identity can drain, capping damage.
